Troubleshooting

Saiem Gilani

Source: vignettes/troubleshooting.Rmd
troubleshooting.Rmd
On this page
library(sdvplotR)

A team does not resolve

A value sdvplotR cannot match becomes NA, with one warning per call that names each value and why it failed:

sdv_resolve(c("KC", "Kansas Cty"), league = "nfl")
#> Warning in sdv_resolve(c("KC", "Kansas Cty"), league = "nfl"): 1 value did not resolve to a "nfl" team: 'Kansas Cty' (unknown).
#> ℹ Use `sdv_suggest()` for candidates, or `strict = TRUE` to error.
#> [1] "12" NA

Things to try, in order:

  1. Check the league. One abbreviation means different teams in different leagues, so league is required, and it must be one of sdv_leagues(). ESPN’s NBL is "nbl" (ESPN ids), while the DataCore-keyed NBL is "nbl_au".

  2. Ask for candidates. sdv_suggest() ranks the closest names:

    sdv_suggest("Kansas Cty", league = "nfl", n = 3)
#>   team_id               name
#> 1      12 Kansas City Chiefs

  3. Name the id system. The default id_system = "auto" tries the index’s own team_id first, then the provider ids in a fixed order (an ESPN id wins over an equal NCAA id). It never tries "nhl_id", "fox", "cbs", "sports247" or "on3", whose numbers overlap ESPN’s. Pass the provider your values come from:

    sdv_resolve("54", league = "mbb", id_system = "fox")
#> [1] "41"

  4. Pass a season. A code reused across eras resolves to its current holder. The warning says ambiguous when a code fits several teams. season picks the team of that year:

    # the Quebec Nordiques: the franchise's team_id, today the Colorado Avalanche
sdv_resolve("QUE", league = "nhl", season = 1990)
#> [1] "17"

  5. Look the team up. sdv_teams(league) lists every team and its team_id, and sdv_aliases(league) every spelling each id system holds. The Leagues and Identifiers article explains what the ids are in each league.

In a pipeline where a miss should stop the run, use strict = TRUE. It raises an error of class sdvplotR_unresolved instead of warning:

res <- tryCatch(
  sdv_resolve("Kansas Cty", league = "nfl", strict = TRUE),
  sdvplotR_unresolved = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
res
#> [1] "\033[1m\033[22m1 value did not resolve to a \033[34m\"nfl\"\033[39m team: 'Kansas Cty' (unknown)."

A logo or wordmark is missing

sdv_logo_url() returns NA with a warning where a team does not resolve or has no mark of that kind. The geoms leave that point blank. Check the URL directly, and list the marks the archive holds with sdv_marks():

sdv_logo_url(c("KC", "Kansas Cty"), "nfl")
#> Warning in sdv_logo_url(c("KC", "Kansas Cty"), "nfl"): 1 value did not resolve to a "nfl" team: 'Kansas Cty' (unknown).
#> ℹ Use `sdv_suggest()` for candidates, or `strict = TRUE` to error.
#> [1] "https://sdv.nyc3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets/public/sha256/3d/3d77958dc6373768919bb2681cbe1b143f56c07a1f013460def665a5026a7f3d.png"
#> [2] NA
head(sdv_marks("KC", "nfl")[, c("team_id", "variant", "mark_type")])
#>   team_id              variant mark_type
#> 1      12   primary_logo_white      logo
#> 2      12 secondary_logo_white      logo
#> 3      12                 dark      logo
#> 4      12              default      logo
#> 5      12           scoreboard      logo
#> 6      12      scoreboard_dark      logo
  • A variant the team lacks falls back to its closest mark of the same polarity. A variant no team in the league has is an error that lists the league’s variants.
  • Not every league has wordmarks (mark_type = "wordmark"), and older seasons have logos only where the archive dates its marks.
  • Team logos and headshots are downloaded when the plot draws, and cached for the session by ‘ggpath’. With no network, the plot draws without them.

A headshot is missing

Headshots are keyed by player id, and id_system says whose. The default is id_system = "espn" (the ESPN athlete id). Other options:

  • "league": the league’s own id, such as the MLBAM id, the NHL API id, or HockeyTech’s player_id for the HockeyTech leagues, which have no ESPN photos.
  • "gsis": NFL GSIS ids.
  • A provider’s player id ("fox", "yahoo", "cbs", "kenpom", "ncaa" and others, by league), which maps to the player’s ESPN id.

?sdv_headshot_url has the full table of leagues and id systems. Things to know:

  • ESPN and league ids are plain digits, so an id from the wrong system draws the wrong player or no image rather than an error.
  • An id the provider maps do not hold is NA.
  • For an id with no photo, the NBA, WNBA, MLB and NHL CDNs serve a silhouette. ESPN and HockeyTech answer 404: the ggplot geoms skip that player with a warning, and the gt, reactable and ggtext helpers show a broken image.
  • The NBA and WNBA CDNs refuse requests from datacenter IPs, so a plot drawn on CI or a server can come back without those headshots.
  • Leagues outside that table have no headshots: the international basketball and European hockey leagues, cricket and F1 among them.

The data looks out of date

sdvplotR reads the team index and the logo manifest from the SportsDataverse CDN and keeps them on disk for a day (in tools::R_user_dir("sdvplotR", "cache")). sdv_versions() reports what the session has loaded and where it came from:

sdv_versions()
#> $package
#> [1] "0.3.0"
#> 
#> $index_version
#> [1] "abd1a34c1550"
#> 
#> $index_source
#> [1] "snapshot"
#> 
#> $manifest_rows
#> [1] 48650
#> 
#> $manifest_source
#> [1] "snapshot"

index_source is "live" (the CDN, or the disk copy within a day of it), "cache" (an older disk copy, after a failed refresh) or "snapshot" (the copy bundled with the package). To read the CDN again now, turn offline mode off if you set it (the snapshot is always used while it is on), then clear the caches:

options(sdvplotR.offline = FALSE)
sdv_clear_cache()
sdv_versions()

options(sdvplotR.offline = TRUE), set before the first lookup, keeps the session on the bundled snapshot. Use it for reproducible builds and machines with no network. On CRAN, and in an R CMD check with NOT_CRAN unset, the package uses the snapshot on its own (devtools::check() sets NOT_CRAN=true, so it reads the CDN).

Saving an image fails

Saving a gt table, or a grid or stack of them, to PNG goes through the ‘webshot2’ package and a headless Chrome. Install ‘webshot2’, and check that chromote::find_chrome() returns a path that exists. ggplot2 plots save with ggplot2::ggsave() as usual.

A playing surface fails

sdv_surface() draws its courts, fields and rinks through ‘sportyR’ (>= 2.4.5), which is a suggested package. If it is missing or older, sdv_surface() offers to install it. An older ‘sportyR’ that is already loaded stays loaded until R restarts, and sdv_surface() says so: restart R after updating it.

Still stuck?

Open an issue on GitHub with the call, the warning and the output of sdv_versions(). A wrong logo or color for a team is a data issue, fixed upstream in the team index: the issue form has a template for it.
